title: procurement-tools spec-as-code
description: Machine-readable requirement set for one purchase or one market survey. Written as YAML (spec.yaml), validated and rendered by scripts/spec_tools.py. Requirement IDs are stable across revisions and are the join key used by conformance records, BOM lines and RFQ line items.

spec_version.description: Version of THIS file format, not of the spec. Currently 1.

id.description: Stable slug for the spec, e.g. 'laser-measure-2026-08'. Referenced by conformance records and BOM lines.

revision.description: Increments on every change that alters what would pass. Conformance records pin the revision they were evaluated against, so a bump invalidates nothing silently.

status.description: frozen = no further changes while a purchase is in flight. superseded = a later spec replaces it; name it in supersedes_note.

scope.description: What is being specified, in capability terms. Vendor-neutral: no product may appear here.

out_of_scope.description: What this spec deliberately does NOT constrain. Load-bearing: it stops incidental attributes of an example product being promoted to requirements downstream.

destination.description: Address profile id, matching addresses.yaml used by price-scan.

id.description: Allocated sequentially and NEVER reused, even after retirement. This is the join key across every other artefact.

title.description: Short column header for the matrix. Defaults to a truncation of the statement.

kind.description: must = disqualifying if absent. must-not = disqualifying if present. nice = tie-breaker, never disqualifies and never scores.

statement.description: The requirement in one sentence, phrased as a property of the product rather than of a purchase. Written so a subagent that has never seen this repo can judge it.

parameter.description: The measurable attribute, when there is one, e.g. 'bluetooth_profile', 'max_range', 'ip_rating'.

operator.description: Only meaningful alongside parameter. Makes the requirement checkable rather than arguable.

verify.description: The evidence class that SETTLES this requirement. Anything weaker leaves the cell unknown rather than passing it.

evidence.description: What specifically would settle it — the datasheet field, the manual section, the standard clause, the question to ask the vendor. This is the sentence a research subagent acts on.

rejects.description: Evidence that looks sufficient and is not. Retail bullet points, marketing copy, a spec repeated across roundups from one wrong original.

rationale.description: Why this is required. Read when deciding whether to relax it.

added_in.description: Spec revision this requirement first appeared in.

retired.description: Requirements are retired, never deleted, so historic conformance records stay interpretable.
